angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 2,540,001 km at 47.55 pc = 0.71 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 77233: distance 47.551 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.012), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 47.551 +/- 0.571 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 21.5924 +/- 0.3070 mas (same row, RUWE 3.53), 70.3 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 3.651 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 77233: radius 3.651 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 59.598 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.118) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 2,540,001 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 8399 +/- 526 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 77233: effective temperature 8399 +/- 526 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.045) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 77233: effective temperature 8399 +/- 526 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.045) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 727) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 3.45 from 2023ApJS..266...11B; the 1 published value span log g 3.4522 to 3.4522, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.0% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJS..266...11B)
